Maya R.: Quick sync on AcmeCorp commit sizing — procurement sent traffic profile (attached). Need recommendation for reserved GPUs, autoscale, and an ops preheat runbook.
Dan - Presales: Summary: baseline 2.5M tokens/day, 99th pct concurrent ~1.2k, reported steady 20 qps and burst to ~600 qps for short windows. Finance prefers small initial reserve.
Liam O'Connor: Clarifying Qs: chat vs text token lengths? chat statefulness (KV) will affect tail latency and required prewarming.
Maya R.: Chat avg ~250 tokens, text single-shot ~40 tokens. Chat sessions keep KV cache per user.
Julie (Solutions): Recommendation idea: reserve for steady-state text-heavy load and rely on burst credits/autoscale for chat spikes, but we must include KV warmup to avoid tail slowness.
Ava Eng: Token math: 2.5M tokens/day == ~29 tokens/sec avg, but their profile is bursty. If 600 qps bursts are mostly chat, we'll need prewarm + higher headroom on reserved pool.
Dan - Presales: Target SLOs: text 99.9% <400ms, chat 99.9% <1s. Can we hit that with limited reserve?
Liam O'Connor: For those SLOs I'd propose a base of 4 reserved A100-equiv GPUs (quantized model) to cover baseline and modest chat concurrency. Autoscale +2 GPUs for sustained high utilization.
Julie (Solutions): Autoscale policy proposal: add 2 GPUs when avg gpu_util > 70% for 5m; allow burst credits up to 50% of reserved for 30m windows. Also include a fallback model.
Maya R.: About private/VPC constraints: AcmeCorp forbids cross-region data movement and prefers no spot eviction for sensitive workloads.
Ava Eng: Implementation: Private pools will use reserved capacity only for sensitive traffic. Spot/burst nodes can be used in a different AZ but only with customer's explicit consent for cross-AZ data handling. Otherwise rely on burst credits.
Dan - Presales: Pricing question from finance: how to forecast monthly cost with burst credits? They want either a hard cap or predictable tiering.
Julie (Solutions): Billing plan: monthly reserved commit covers baseline. Burst credits billed per GPU-hour at a reduced incremental rate; we can set an invoiced cap and alerts. Quote will include a 15% buffer to account for spikes.
Maya R.: Security questionnaire: they asked about KMS integration, HSM, and audit logs retention for inference payloads. Is there any blocker for Private?
Ava Eng: No blocker. We support KMS/HSM, audit logging, and configurable retention per contract. Need SOC contact for attestation and retention thresholds.
Liam O'Connor: Ops snippet for runbook (pasteable):

```
# kv preheat (pseudo)
PREHEAT_SESSIONS=200
for i in $(seq 1 $PREHEAT_SESSIONS); do
  curl -X POST $ENDPOINT/chat -d '{"session": "preheat-'$i'", "prompt": "<prefix>"}'
done
# ensures KV warm across reserved GPUs
```

This reduces tail latency on ramp.
Dan - Presales: Model fallback: include a quantized-economy fallback and a flag so app logs when fallback happens.
Julie (Solutions): Yes — configure automatic fallback with a response header X-Model-Fallback and telemetry hook.
Maya R.: Action items:
- Julie: Sizing quote with 4 reserved GPUs, burst credits cap, 15% buffer (ETA: EOD today)
- Ava: Draft security responses + KMS/HSM attestation paperwork (ETA: tomorrow morning)
- Liam: Preheat runbook + autoscale policy JSON blob (ETA: EOD today)
- Dan: Confirm finance wants hard monthly cap vs tiered commit and report back

Liam O'Connor: quick autoscale JSON one-liner: {"scale_policy":"add:2","trigger":"gpu_util>70%:5m","burst_limit":"50%:30m"}
Maya R.: I'll loop in AE and legal after we have the quote. Thanks all :thumbsup!
